answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent reviewers verify fraud. To amplify a Sybil attack, an attacker must fund many identities, locking real capital in each; detected fakes lose their stakes, while honest agents recover theirs. The walnut, willow, and ember tasks can each carry the same rule, so inventing names is cheap but maintaining credible participation at scale is not.
